source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC-Web -> Overview.
2. Check Server information.
3. Click "View more" to check.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: All information should match SPEC definition.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES offers a useful read-only ComputerSystem lookup but assumes `system` as ComputerSystemId, disables TLS verification, exposes reusable credentials and narrows `all information` to Model/Serial. It also bypasses the required Overview and `View more` controls, so successful JSON cannot prove the source workflow or complete SPEC coverage.

This review further requires Systems collection discovery, explicit summary-versus-detail coverage and three-way UI/API/authoritative-SPEC identity correlation without an automatic re-read.

historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves Overview and View-more as the original method; ED-34 treats the field matrix and expected values as Project readiness rather than permanent blockage; ED-35 records Redfish as corroboration and rejects API-only substitution; ED-38 requires trusted identity, protected credentials, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify every Project-defined Server information field shown in both the BMC Overview summary and its `View more` detail view represents the intended physical server and matches the authoritative Project SPEC/asset recipe.
original_method: On the identified BMC WebUI build and approved role, capture the Server information summary, select `View more` once and capture the complete detail field set. Compare each required UI field with its signed SPEC value and, where defined, the corresponding property from the discovered Redfish ComputerSystem or linked inventory resource.
manual_activity: The Project owner supplies the authoritative server-information matrix and approves handling of serial, asset and identity data. Browser/API automation can collect and compare defined fields, while an engineer resolves vendor-derived or visually truncated values and owns the final judgment.
required_inputs: Exact target BMC and physical server identity, certificate, firmware and WebUI build
Signed field matrix listing every required Overview and View-more label, expected value, formatting/case rule, authoritative source and sensitivity classification
Expected account role, locale, viewport, View-more selector/route and loading-complete behavior
Discovered Redfish Systems member URI with evidence binding it to the target chassis/server rather than an assumed `system` member
Vendor mapping for fields stored on ComputerSystem, Chassis, Managers, Assembly, OEM or other linked resources plus freshness/stale rules
Protected authentication, redaction/masking policy and approved handling for absent, unknown, not-applicable or permission-filtered values
safety_requirements: Do not assume `/redfish/v1/Systems/system`; enumerate the Systems collection and bind the selected ComputerSystem to the intended physical server using approved identifiers before comparing data.
Do not use `curl -k` as the formal path or expose credentials in process listings/transcripts. Require trusted TLS and protected session/secret handling for both UI and Redfish.
Do not equate Model/Serial JSON with `all information`. The accepted result requires the Project's explicit complete field matrix and separate evidence for Overview summary and View-more detail.
Redact or tokenize serial numbers, asset tags, UUIDs and other customer identifiers in general artifacts while retaining a controlled comparison capable of detecting mismatch.
Do not trigger inventory refresh, rescan, synchronization, edits or configuration changes. Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL or audit logs merely to create a baseline.

Perform each read/navigation once; stop without automatic retry on wrong-system evidence, identity ambiguity, stale or mixed data, unexpected mutation, missing required fields or inability to protect sensitive values.
agent_execution_scope: Establish the BMC-to-server binding and read the Systems collection before selecting a ComputerSystem member; record `@odata.id`, schema type and stable identity evidence.
Capture the Overview summary first, then invoke the exact `View more` control once and wait for the documented detail-ready state without changing inventory.
Build a per-field comparison across summary UI, detail UI, mapped Redfish/linked resources and the signed SPEC, preserving raw values in a controlled artifact and redacted reporting copies.
Report missing, extra, truncated, stale, permission-filtered and mismatched fields individually; preserve logs and never issue DUT PASS/FAIL or retry automatically.
engineer_actions: Approve the exhaustive field/value/source/sensitivity matrix and the identity evidence that binds the BMC and ComputerSystem to the physical SUT.
Approve vendor/OEM mappings, UI formatting equivalences, unavailable-value rules, role variants and any fields intentionally omitted from general evidence.
Review the field-by-field comparison and summary/detail navigation evidence, then issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It can read a vendor deployment whose member happens to be `system`, but that ID is not source-specified and cannot be assumed. The command bypasses the WebUI workflow, covers only some likely fields, disables TLS verification and provides no SPEC comparison, so it does not satisfy this testcase.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using trusted TLS and protected authentication, enumerate `/redfish/v1/Systems`, select the ComputerSystem explicitly bound to the target server, and GET it plus only the mapped linked resources. In parallel, capture Overview and View-more fields and compare all three sources against the approved matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Overview, `View more`, all-information SPEC criterion, absent Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Redfish is supplemental evidence rather than a replacement.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Drive the exact summary-to-detail UI path, discover the correct ComputerSystem resource, normalize only engineer-approved presentation differences and produce a row-per-field UI/API/SPEC comparison with controlled handling of sensitive identifiers.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact physical SUT, BMC firmware/WebUI build and account role selected by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record ComputerSystem `@odata.type`, BMC firmware and UI build because available properties, OEM extensions and screen fields vary by implementation.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: DMTF Redfish ComputerSystem schema/data model, vendor UI-to-resource mapping, signed Project SPEC and asset/configuration recipe.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains both required UI views and supplies a reproducible complete comparison; corrects the assumed Redfish member and unsafe transport/credential handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: ComputerSystem-only evidence may omit chassis, manager, FRU, assembly or OEM fields; UI-only evidence may be truncated, localized or stale; only the approved mapping establishes `all information` coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target binding, field matrix, UI paths, Redfish/OEM mapping, SPEC values, role, formatting, freshness and sensitivity rules.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong BMC/System pairing can create a convincing false match; inventory caches can mix ages; sensitive identifiers can leak through screenshots or raw JSON.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a vendor inventory API, host DMI or an asset database instead of or alongside Redfish, but must retain the Overview and View-more UI checkpoints, document each field's source and freshness, obtain engineer approval and disclose any Master field coverage not verified. A new tool is not a blocker by itself.
expected_evidence: Trusted BMC endpoint/certificate, controller firmware/WebUI build, physical server identity and selected ComputerSystem `@odata.id`/schema evidence
Signed Project field matrix with expected values, authoritative source, normalization rule and sensitivity label
Redacted Overview summary and View-more detail screenshots/DOM/routes with role, locale, viewport, loading state and timestamps
Per-field UI-summary/UI-detail/Redfish-or-vendor-source/SPEC table including exact, missing, extra, truncated, stale, redacted and permission-filtered outcomes
Controlled proof for serial/asset/UUID comparisons plus redacted shareable artifacts and resource freshness/ETag metadata where available
Proof no inventory state or logs changed, explicit uncovered fields/limitations and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require Server information in Overview and View more to match the SPEC. The Master leaves the field list open, and DeepSeek narrows it to a fixed API resource, but neither creates a contradiction in the source identity or purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The UI workflow and comparison purpose are clear. The exact field list, values, System URI, vendor mapping and redaction policy are expected Project readiness inputs, so the case remains PACKAGE rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE, replaces the assumed fixed URI and insecure API-only evidence with collection discovery plus source-faithful Overview/View-more and exhaustive SPEC mapping.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its hybrid field-matrix approach and strengthens physical-System binding, summary/detail separation, controlled sensitive-value evidence and no-retry behavior.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces direct-run acceptance of a partial API dump with a complete, identity-bound UI/API/SPEC comparison.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a partial Model/Serial payload from being called `all information`, prevents a guessed Redfish member or wrong server from passing, and preserves the required `View more` UI coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Server identity spans multiple layers: the Overview may show a curated subset, the detail view may add fields, and Redfish can distribute properties across ComputerSystem and linked/OEM resources. A comparison is meaningful only after the BMC and selected System are bound to the physical SUT and each displayed field is mapped to an authoritative SPEC entry. Raw JSON volume is not coverage, and sensitive identifiers require controlled rather than omitted comparison.
